title: Dualizing complexes after finite coefficient extension
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $X$ be Noetherian, and let $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] be dualizing: $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] preserves that category and its evaluation-transpose biduality maps are isomorphisms. For every commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra $A$, put $K_A=A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. For general $A$, bounded constructible means bounded cohomology admitting a finite locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finitely generated $A$-module stalks; finite Tor amplitude means that derived tensor with every $A$-module sheaf in degree zero has cohomology in one fixed finite interval. Then $K_A$ is bounded constructible and $R\mathcal Hom_A(-,K_A)$ preserves the bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, with natural isomorphisms given by their evaluation-transpose biduality maps. In particular, when $A$ is a finite field, this applies to all of $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. For $N\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, the canonical internal-Hom base-change identifications for $A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}N$ identify its biduality map with $A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(N\to D_KD_KN)$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Theorem 7.1.3 and Definition 7.1.1; Theorem 7.6.1 for the canonical internal-Hom coefficient comparison and its use in the proof of 7.1.3 (printed pp. 300–301, 310–311)

proof.text: Choose $[a,b]$ containing the cohomology of $K$. At a geometric stalk a complex of $\Lambda$-vector spaces splits into its cohomology and contractible summands. Extension to $A$ therefore has cohomology $A\otimes_\Lambda H^i(K_{\bar x})$ in the same interval; tensoring further with any $A$-module $V$ gives $H^i(K_{\bar x})\otimes_\Lambda V$, still in that interval. The tensor identification [lem-sfb-etale-derived-tensor-stalk] and exact conservative stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact, lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] give this bound for tensor with every module sheaf. Extension over the field is exact, so $\mathcal H^i(K_A)=A_X\otimes_{\Lambda_X}\mathcal H^i(K)$; on a finite common constructible stratification this is locally constant with finite free $A$-stalks. Thus $K_A\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. The same stalk calculation over any field $B/\Lambda$ proves $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)=D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Theorem 7.1.3, p. 311: membership of K_A in D^b_ctf, specialized to field Lambda

proof.text: The given $K$ witnesses the duality-existence hypothesis of [lem-per-ctf-hom-coefficient-comparison]. Its first conclusion applied to $(M,K_A)$ gives $D_AM=R\mathcal Hom_A(M,K_A)\in D^b_{ctf}$ for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}$, and a second application gives $D_A^2M\in D^b_{ctf}$. The same node gives the evaluation-defined natural coefficient comparisons for these pairs along every map of Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebras. For $\Lambda\to A$ it applies to $(N,K)$ and $(D_KN,K)$, since the original duality makes both $N$ and $D_KN$ bounded constructible over the field.

source.place: XVII, Theorem 7.6.1 and proof of Theorem 7.1.3, pp. 310-311

proof.text: Compute the actual biduality morphism under coefficient extension. Write $R\to S$ for a map of Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebras, $T=S_X\otimes^L_{R_X}(-)$, $K_S=TK_R$ and $D_R=R\mathcal Hom_R(-,K_R)$. For $M,K_R,D_RM$ in $D^b_{ctf}$ let $\alpha_M:TD_RM\xrightarrow{\sim}D_STM$ be the comparison of [lem-per-ctf-hom-coefficient-comparison]. Identify $TD_R^2M$ with $D_S^2TM$ by $$\beta_M=R\mathcal Hom_S(\alpha_M^{-1},1)\circ\alpha_{D_RM,K_R}.$$ The tensor--Hom transpose of $\beta_M T(\delta_M)$ is $T(\mathrm{ev}_R)\circ(1\otimes\alpha_M^{-1})$, using the signed symmetry in $\delta$. The defining equation $\mathrm{ev}_S\circ(1\otimes\alpha_M)=T(\mathrm{ev}_R)$ for $\alpha_M$ shows that this transpose is $\mathrm{ev}_S$. Uniqueness of transposes gives $\beta_M T(\delta_M)=\delta_{TM}$. Taking $R=\Lambda$, $S=A$, $M=N$, $K_R=K$ proves the final clause of the item. All comparisons are natural, so the identity is natural in $M$.

source.place: XVII, Definition 7.1.1 and canonical coefficient comparison of Theorem 7.6.1, pp. 310-311

proof.text: First treat an arbitrary field extension $B/\Lambda$, including infinite $B$. Step 1 identifies $D^b_c$ with $D^b_{ctf}$ and Step 2 gives preservation by $D_B$. Let $\mathcal T$ be the class where $\delta_M:M\to D_B^2M$ is invertible. By [lem-sf-hom-triangulated], applying $D_B$ twice gives an exact covariant functor: the two reversals of a distinguished triangle restore its order. The natural evaluation-transpose maps form a morphism to this double-dual triangle, with the signed shift identifications. The cohomology long exact sequences of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] then show that invertibility on two terms implies invertibility on the third. The shift identification sends $\delta_{M[r]}$ to $\delta_M[r]$ (the two contravariant shift signs cancel). Additivity gives the direct-sum property; naturality on the inclusion and projection of a retract makes its biduality map a retract of the original one, hence invertible. Thus $\mathcal T$ is closed under shifts, cones, finite sums and direct summands.

source.place: XVII, proof of Theorem 7.1.2 in 7.5.3, p. 310: devissage of the biduality property

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-prime-field-tensor-devissage] with $A=B$. Each generator $N_X\otimes^L_\Lambda F$ has $N$ finite-dimensional over $B$. A finite $B$-basis identifies it with a finite sum of copies of $B_X\otimes^L_\Lambda F$. Step 3 identifies the latter's biduality with $B_X\otimes^L_\Lambda\delta_F$, an isomorphism because $K$ is dualizing. Every generator is therefore in $\mathcal T$. Step 4 and the generation statement give $\mathcal T=D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. This proves field-coefficient biduality without asserting that every individual $B$-complex descends to $\Lambda$.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 7.4.6 and proof of 7.4.1, pp. 307-308, in the argument of 7.5.3

proof.text: For general $A$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let $B=A/\mathfrak m$ for a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-per-ctf-hom-coefficient-comparison], coefficient extension gives a finite-Tor constructible $B$-complex $B_X\otimes_A^LM$. Tensor associativity identifies $B_X\otimes_A^LK_A$ with $K_B$. Step 3 identifies $B_X\otimes_A^L\delta_M$ with its biduality map over the field $B$, so Step 5 makes it invertible. Let $C$ be a cone of $\delta_M$. Exactness of derived tensor [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated] gives $B_X\otimes_A^LC=0$ for every maximal ideal. The residue field $B$ need not be finite; this is why Step 5 allowed arbitrary fields.

source.place: XVII, proof of Theorem 7.1.3, p. 311: reduction modulo maximal ideals

proof.text: The cone $C$ has bounded cohomology with finite geometric stalks as $A$-modules. Indeed, Step 2 gives this for $M,D_A^2M$, and [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] expresses each cohomology stalk of $C$ as an extension of a cokernel by a kernel between finitely generated $A$-modules; $A$ is Noetherian. Exact stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] give $C_{\bar x}\in D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] makes it pseudo-coherent. By [lem-sfb-etale-derived-tensor-stalk], its derived tensor with each maximal residue field is zero. For each integer $i$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-pseudocoherent-maximal-fibre-perfect] with $a=b=i+1$: its fiber-vanishing hypothesis holds, and its conclusion with the module $A$ gives $H^i(C_{\bar x})=0$. Every stalk of every cohomology sheaf of $C$ is zero. Exactness and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] imply $C=0$, hence $\delta_M$ is invertible.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 7.6.2 and proof of Theorem 7.1.3, p. 311; realized using existing Stacks 066E and 068V interfaces

proof.text: Steps 1, 2 and 7 give bounded constructibility of $K_A$ and preservation and natural evaluation-transpose biduality on $D^b_{ctf}$. If $A$ is a finite field, Step 1 identifies this category with all of $D^b_c$; finite generation over $A$ is equivalent to finiteness of the stalks as sets, as in the original finite-coefficient definition. Step 3 is the required identity on inputs extended from $\Lambda$.

proof_origin.place: Adapted from XVII, proof of Theorem 7.1.3, p. 311, and the tensor-generator devissage of 7.5.3, p. 310; existing 066E/068V realize residue detection.
